question: Why do different health workers come together as a team in community health?

options.A: To address complex health and social needs
options.B: To place full control of care on physicians
options.C: To reduce the number of working nurses
options.D: To lower the cost of running hospital wards

explanation: You've got this! Community health involves many overlapping social and physical issues, so different experts team up to tackle them all together. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h1)

question: In community health, why can't just one type of health worker solve every problem?

options.B: Doctors lack the training to visit local neighborhoods
options.C: Nurses refuse to handle community cases on their own
options.D: Community issues involve physical, social, and economic factors

explanation: Spot on! Because a patient's health is tied to housing, money, and food, we need a mix of specialists to truly help. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h1)

question: What is the most important ingredient for any healthcare team to work well together?

options.A: Strict orders given only by physicians
options.D: Mutual respect among all team members

explanation: Great thinking! Teamwork only works when everyone values what each person brings to the table. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h2)

question: A nurse and a social worker disagree on how to discharge an elderly patient who lives alone. What should guide their next step?

options.A: Following the nurse's plan because nurses spend more time at the bedside
options.B: Letting the patient leave without any support services
options.C: Focusing on the patient's needs through shared decision-making
options.D: Escalating the disagreement to the hospital director immediately

explanation: Exactly! When team members see things differently, putting the patient's welfare first and talking it through always points the way forward. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h2)

question: What is the main job of a social worker on a community health team?

options.A: Reviewing lab results for abnormal electrolyte levels
options.B: Connecting families to housing and financial support
options.C: Performing surgical procedures in the clinic
options.D: Prescribing medications for high blood pressure

explanation: You got it! Social workers are pros at linking patients to resources outside the clinic that make daily life easier. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h3)

question: Why is it important for community health workers to know each other's roles clearly?

options.A: To reduce the number of home visits required each week
options.B: To prevent missed tasks and avoid doing the exact same work
options.C: To allow nurses to prescribe medications legally
options.D: To ensure doctors maintain authority over all other workers

explanation: Well done! Knowing who does what keeps care smooth and ensures no important patient need slips through the cracks. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h3)

question: In the SBAR communication tool, what does the letter 'B' stand for?
explanation: Awesome! 'B' is for Background, which gives the history and context leading up to the current situation. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h4)

question: Why are structured tools like SBAR so helpful for community health teams?

options.A: Government regulations require every home visit to be recorded on video
options.B: Printed records are completely banned in rural clinics
options.C: Team members work in different locations and need clear, quick updates
options.D: Patients refuse to speak with doctors unless a nurse is present

explanation: Spot on! Since community staff operate out in the field, quick and clear updates keep everyone on the same page. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h4)

question: How is a multidisciplinary care plan different from a plan made by just one health worker?

options.A: It removes the need for nursing assessments completely
options.B: It allows the patient to change medical diagnoses at any time
options.C: It combines insights from various fields into one unified set of goals
options.D: It focuses exclusively on hospital discharge procedures

explanation: You're doing great! A team plan blends nursing, social work, and medical insights so every angle of the patient's health is covered. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h5)

question: A patient is finding it hard to follow a strict diet and exercise plan. What should the team do?

options.A: Double the medication dose without telling the patient
options.B: Re-evaluate the plan with the patient to fit their actual lifestyle
options.C: Discharge the patient from community care for non-compliance
options.D: Report the patient to local law enforcement authorities

explanation: Exactly! If a plan isn't working, we adjust it together with the patient so it fits their real life and is easy to follow. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to good teamwork?
explanation: Correct! Open communication helps a team thrive—it's definitely not a barrier! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h6)

question: What happens when healthcare workers operate in isolated silos within a community?

options.A: Treatment plans become much easier for patients to follow
options.B: Every professional automatically knows what the others are doing
options.C: Patient care becomes fragmented and important details are missed
options.D: Healthcare costs drop significantly for local families

explanation: Spot on! Working in isolation means communication breaks down, leaving gaps that can hurt patient care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h6)

question: Which of these is a standard way to check if a community health team is doing a good job?

options.A: Number of desks in the clinic

explanation: You've got it! Lower readmission rates usually mean the community team is doing a stellar job keeping people well at home. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h7)

question: Why is continuous quality improvement important after putting a team care plan in place?

options.A: To punish team members who make minor documentation errors
options.B: To increase the paperwork burden for community nurses
options.C: To identify weaknesses and update processes for better patient results
options.D: To prove to the government that the clinic has extra funding

explanation: Brilliant! Quality improvement is all about learning and growing so we can give our patients better care every single day. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h7)
